newsitem.title: PERU: Peru legislator wants Carter to mediate siege.
newsitem.headline: Peru legislator wants Carter to mediate siege.

text.p: An opposition legislator urged Peru's government on Friday to ask former U.S. president Jimmy Carter to mediate in negotiations with Marxist rebels holding 74 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
Congressman Harold Forsyth said President Alberto Fujimori should invite Carter because without outside intervention the crisis would "drag on several more days without concrete progress."

Carter, who has acted as a trouble-shooter in various international crises, might be acceptable to the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas because of his support for a campaign to gain a retrial for an American woman, Lori Berenson, jailed as an alleged MRTA member.

Forsyth's proposal received no immediate response from Fujimori, who has flatly rejected the rebels' demands that he free all their jailed comrades and improve conditions for prisoners sentenced on terrorism charges.
Judges wearing hoods in a secret military court sentenced Berenson in December 1995 to life imprisonment for allegedly helping to plot a takeover of Congress.
Her conviction and harsh conditions at Peru's Yanamayo maximum-security prison have prompted foreign criticism of Peru's treatment of guerrillas during trial and imprisonment.
